subject.title: fix: warn when transcript byte guard is inactive

question: Should this PR intentionally make inactive maxActiveTranscriptBytes configs emit config warnings and default Doctor lint findings?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and correct, but accepting a new default warning can affect operators who gate upgrades or automation on warning-free Doctor lint output.

options.title: Accept the diagnostic
options.body: Merge the PR as the deliberate compatibility-visible warning for configs that were previously silently ineffective.

options.title: Make Doctor lint opt-in
options.body: Keep the config warning but require the Doctor health check to be default-disabled if warning-free lint upgrades matter more.

options.title: Pause for warning policy
options.body: Pause only if maintainers want a different warning path, copy, or rollout policy before exposing it to existing operators.

recommendation.title: Accept the diagnostic
recommendation.body: Merge the PR as the deliberate compatibility-visible warning for configs that were previously silently ineffective.

likelyOwner.reason: The byte guard and documented truncateAfterCompaction requirement appear to originate from steipete's commit, making him the strongest owner for accepting the diagnostic policy.
